title: A Fish Leaps at 37 mph and Has Killed People Like a Spear

scenes.text: Pacific night fishermen fear a fish that never bites.
The needlefish: up to a metre long, a beak full of teeth, and short jumps of up to 60 kilometres an hour.
Shine a light on the water at night and whole schools launch themselves straight at it.
In 1977 a ten-year-old boy fishing in Hawaii was killed by one. In 2024 a surfer in Indonesia died the same way.
The beak can snap off inside the wound. It isn't hunting you. It's a living javelin thrown at the light.
So no, the fish never bites. It doesn't have to.

description:
Needlefish never bite people, yet they have killed several: they jump at up to 60 km/h (37 mph), are drawn to lights at night, and their sharp beaks can pierce a chest or a neck.
A 10-year-old boy was killed by a leaping needlefish in Hawaii in 1977; a surfer died in Indonesia in October 2024; other deaths are recorded in Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines.
Would you still night-fish with a lamp?
thumbnail_text: A FISH. 37 MPH. A LIVING SPEAR
subject: needlefish
first_comment: Needlefish leap at a shallow angle to ambush small fish, and a bright lamp at night sends whole schools flying at the boat. Which animal kills by accident, not on purpose?
